messages:
oncall-bot: SEV2 alert — kv-pool-12 (us-west1) showing repeated container restarts and OOMs. Auto-scale + pager triggered. https://incidents.internal/1751236789 :rotating_light:

liza: I'm on it, joining from night shift. Seeing node flaps across 3 pods in the pool. Containers crash then restart, latency spikes for affected customers (eu-west, us-west).

sam: logs from pod kv-12-3 show repeated CUDA failures right before oom: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` then a coredump. Paging + allocator fragmentation look suspicious.

maya: customer-impact: two high-volume customers reported >20% error rate for generation endpoints, attempts to retry hitting fallback models. Support ticket IDs: #3421, #3422. Not yet escalated externally.

liza: quick repro logs (tail):
```
[2025-04-12T02:13:04Z] runtime: alloc slab=attn_paged idx=4219 size=6.7GB
[2025-04-12T02:13:04Z] cuda: kernel launch failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2025-04-12T02:13:04Z] container: panic: runtime OOM after kv-paged alloc
```

sam: confirms pattern: slow KV cache creep -> fragmentation -> kernel illegal address when page table mapping hits corrupted pointer. We've seen this before but it usually manifests slower. This one's faster, likely due to longer sequences from a customer load test.

liza: immediate mitigations — list: 1) scale pool +1 to absorb traffic 2) enable emergency eviction on kv cache for pool 12 3) cordon + reboot the most-flapping node if it doesn't stabilize in 10m.

maya: agreed. I'm toggling emergency eviction now (hotfix flag: runtime.kv.eviction.force=true) and disabling prefix caching for pool-12 traffic. Watching error rate.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled kv-pool-12 from 6->8 nodes.

jason: customer comms: drafted brief to affected customers, noting degraded latency and we are actively mitigating; asking for permission to mention incident ID 1751236789. Can send now or wait for more stable state?

liza: send now (short note + ETA 30m). Keep language focused on mitigation and next updates.

sam: follow-up: patch plan — schedule rollout of allocator guard that checks page pointer validity before kernel launch, small patch to runtime. We cannot deploy full change mid-incident. Need temporary fallback: pin these pods to a conservative allocator mode (no paged attention, fall back to resident attention) while we stabilize. That reduces throughput but should avoid illegal address.

maya: doing the pin now: add annotation `runtime.alloc.mode=conservative` to deployment kv-pool-12-rollout.

liza: node status after eviction toggle: error rate dropped to ~12% from 28%. Two pods still flapping but not immediately crashing. Latency improving.

sam: request to infra for a rolling reboot of node us-west1-n3 (highest crash count). Reboot helps clear stale device state that can trigger illegal address on subsequent kernels.

infra-bot: reboot scheduled: us-west1-n3 -> now. Expected pod reschedule ~2m.

jason: sent initial customer note. Customers acknowledged, requesting postmortem timeline.

liza: postmortem notes to collect: sequence length distribution during spike, kv cache growth curves, allocator histograms, GPU driver versions, container coredumps. Assigning ownership: sam for runtime traces, maya for infra and autoscaler, jason for customer comms and SLO impact numbers.

sam: also capturing gdb backtrace from coredump and nvcrash logs. If we confirm corrupted pointers, we'll need to rollback paged-attention for affected model variants and push quick allocator guard release.

maya: node reboot completed, pods rescheduled. One formerly-flapping pod recovered and is stable. Monitoring for 10m.

liza: current status (02:45Z): incident in mitigation, major customers degraded but error rate halved. Continuing watch. Will escalate to SEV1 if crash count increases.

oncall-bot: Incident watcher: next automated check at 1751237400. Please update thread with any config flips or customer-facing messages. :eyes:
